thread:
incidents-bot: PAGER — smart-routing anomaly detected. Sudden spike in quality regression metric (qa_rate) for routes using cost-led policy. Potential misroute to 'lite-v2-8bit' variant. Paging @eric_oncall :rotating_light:

eric_oncall: On it. Jumping in — can someone post quick symptom summary?

maya_prod: Customers reporting hallucinations and bad completions for structured prompts (invoices, confirmations). Error rate for those flows up ~12% in last 10m.

raj_sre: Observed routing changes 12:03Z — weight shift to lite-v2-8bit on cost-led policy after scheduled policy refresh. There was a rollout that increased cheap_variant_score weight. Might be config drift.

luis_platform: Confirming — logs show policy evaluation returned lite-v2-8bit for many sessions that previously hit standard-xlarge-1. Latency improved ~30% but quality dropped.

eric_oncall: Impact: potentially multiple enterprise customers (support list incoming). Severity: likely P1 if escalates. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Pin affected customers to standard-xlarge-1; 2) Set weight 0 for lite-v2-8bit in cost-led policy; 3) Rollback policy to previous revision. Which is fastest?

support_olivia: We have 3 customers with active tickets (acct-447, acct-12b, acct-omega). One is production-critical (acct-447) — they reported live misbundled invoices. They're asking for ETA.

raj_sre: Fastest is set weight 0 for variant and pin route for acct-447. I'll prepare CLI.

eric_oncall: Go for weight set first, then pin for the hot customer. If that doesn't restore quality, we'll rollback.

raj_sre: Running command now:

```
# set the cheap variant weight to 0 in cost-led routing policy
rwctl routing update-policy --name cost-led --set-variant-weight lite-v2-8bit=0 --author "raj_sre"
```

deploy-bot: Executing routing update (job id: rjob-20260315-0042).

deploy-bot: Success — policy cost-led updated. lite-v2-8bit weight=0.

luis_platform: Observability note: routing table updated across regions, but there are a few in-flight cached decisions. Should clear cache for the affected routes.

raj_sre: Clearing routing cache for acct-447 and acct-12b:

```
rwctl routing flush-cache --customer acct-447,acct-12b
```

deploy-bot: Cache flush queued.

maya_prod: Support notified acct-447 and acct-12b — instructing them to test. Can we confirm quality metrics trending back?

eric_oncall: Watching QA rate and sample completions.

(3 minutes pass)

luis_platform: QA rate for affected flows down to normal baseline. Sample checks: acct-447 invoice prompts look correct now.

support_olivia: acct-447 confirms issue resolved for now. They asked what caused this and want a postmortem.

eric_oncall: Cause hypothesis: cost-led policy refresh inadvertently favored lite-v2-8bit due to a recent change in cost scoring heuristics (lowered penalty for memory-bound models). That produced a quality regression when the variant is incompatible with certain prompt types. Also noticed a fallback loop in region-us-west where lite-v2-8bit couldn't access a specific kv-cache and retried region -> caused repeated policy evals.

raj_sre: For the fallback loop, we saw policy evaluation flip between region preference and variant compatibility, creating bouncing decisions. Need to add a compatibility filter so policy won't select variants that fail health checks for a session.

maya_prod: Immediate tasks: 1) Add compatibility filter to routing evaluator. 2) Add a safety gate — minimum quality score threshold for any automatic cost-based promotion. 3) Revert cost-scoring tweak until we validate across eval sets.

eric_oncall: I'll file the incident as SEV-1 (customer-impacting). Putting a short timeline in incident doc. Handing off to @maya_prod to lead postmortem and followups — I'm going offline in 20m.

maya_prod: Taking lead. Assigning owner tasks now.

maya_prod: TODOs assigned:
- raj_sre: revert cost-scoring tweak and add compatibility filter (blocker)
- luis_platform: add health-check gating to policy engine and improve cache invalidation path
- support_olivia: notify impacted customers with root-cause statement once we have a draft
- eric_oncall: keep monitoring until handoff complete

raj_sre: Reverting cost-scoring tweak:

```
rwctl config rollback --key routing.cost_scoring --to-revision 87
```
deploy-bot: Config rollback applied (rev 87).

raj_sre: Implementing compatibility filter branch and tests. ETA ~3h for prod-safe rollout.

luis_platform: I'm going to add an explicit model-compatibility check in the evaluator and a circuit-breaker if repeated failures observed for a session. Also improving logs to capture variant health reasons.

maya_prod: Setting incident channel for postmortem drafting and tracking: #incidents-postmortems. Will schedule a blameless review.

support_olivia: Sending immediate customer comms (holding language): "We identified an automated routing change that briefly sent traffic to a lower-capacity model variant, causing degraded outputs. We've reverted the change and are implementing safeguards." Will send once approved by eng lead.

eric_oncall: Handing off active monitoring to maya. I'll be reachable if needed.

maya_prod: Thanks. I'll keep updates here. Marking incident as mitigated for now but open for follow-ups.

incidents-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=P1, incident_id=INC-20260315-21.

maya_prod: Postmortem owner: maya_prod. Will include timeline, root cause (cost scoring change + missing compatibility gate + cache TTL issues), immediate mitigations performed, and long-term actions (compatibility filter, quality threshold, routing policy review).

raj_sre: Noted for next release: add integration tests that simulate structured prompts and ensure cheap variants don't pass quality thresholds for those routes.

support_olivia: Closing loop with customers after postmortem draft.

maya_prod: Thanks team. Adding final note: avoid changing cost-scoring heuristics without a canary that runs quality evals on representative prompt-sets.

(reacts: :white_check_mark:, :thumbsup:)
